correctness.rationale: Reduction lemma verified: for N=2m reciprocal P, P(e^{iθ})=e^{imθ}U(cosθ) with c0=a_m, ck=2a_{m-k}, integer Chebyshev basis; P(±1) is sum of 2m+1 odd ±1 terms hence odd/nonzero so all unit-circle zeros are conjugate pairs and Z(P) is even; fixing a0=+1 covers class up to global negation. Enumeration size 16+32+...+4096=8176 correct. Counting method is standard exact Sturm V(-1)-V(+1) with gcd multiplicity ladder. Auditor re-ran stdlib replay.py: 9/9 OK. Auditor wrote independent Fraction-based recount from scratch (different division code) and exhaustively re-enumerated all 2^m halves for every N=8..24: minima 2,2,2,6,4,4,6,6,6 and minimizer counts 2,2,2,22,6,2,12,12,8 and full histograms all match zl_table.json exactly; distribution sums equal 2^m in all 9 cases. DRAFT honestly separates proved lemma/standard algebra from computed exact-arithmetic exhaustion; no analytic closed form claimed.

originality.rationale: Live checks confirm gap. Bedert arXiv:2312.04454 poses exact Z_L(N) question for reciprocal Littlewood polynomials, proves Z_L(N)->infinity, surveys finite bounds (Mercer >=1, Mukunda >=3 odd N>=3, Drungilas >=5 odd N>=7 and >=4 even N>=14); full HTML confirms no exact Z_L table or extremal witnesses for N=8..24. Erdelyi 2001.08151 is flat near-skew-reciprocal existence via Rudin-Shapiro (different symmetry, no census). Schmidt 1302.2766 is L4 limits 2/pi, 4/pi^2 for chirp families (different statistic). Hokken 2301.05656 is square-discriminant asymptotics (different invariant). OEIS text search 'reciprocal Littlewood unimodular zeros' returns No results. Finite bound >=4 for even N>=14 does not mechanically imply exact minima (candidate has 4,4 at 16,18 and 6 elsewhere, plus 2,2,2 below bound range and 6 at N=14); minimization over full reciprocal class with witnesses is not recorded or implied.

value.rationale: Headline claim is first exact Z_L(N) table over contiguous even N=8..24 with palindromic ±1 witnesses and exact counts, motivated before computation by recognized Borwein-Erdelyi-Littmann minimum-unimodular-zero question (Bedert Problem 1/Thm 2 lineage, Drungilas/Mukunda/Mercer bounds). Object (reciprocal Littlewood class) and invariant (unimodular-zero minimum) are natural; values 2,2,2,6,4,4,6,6,6 including non-monotone spike at N=14 and dip at 16,18 were not known or mechanically implied; future work on flatness, reciprocal vs skew-reciprocal symmetry, and Mahler-adjacent zero distribution can retrieve precise boundary values and witnesses. This is an eligible exact-invariant census, not textbook restatement, parameter substitution, tiny gain, or unexplained enumeration: witnesses, histograms, and replay script make it independently verifiable and reusable.
